findings.message: This test was meant to prove that projectHours counts a visible week in full, including projects the PM doesn't manage. Its only check on projectHours is `names.size > 1`. Ayesha's direct reports, or any other project she approves, already give her more than one project id, so the check passes even if projectHours goes back to per-entry scope. Fix: find the project of Dinesh's that Ayesha doesn't manage, and assert that projectHours for Ayesha includes that project with Dinesh's hours. Also assert the same project's figure for a viewer who can't see Dinesh's week.
findings.scenario: Put back `visible(viewer, r.user_id, [projectId])` in projectHours. Ayesha still sees more than one project through her other weeks, so the test stays green.

findings.message: The parity test compares only grand totals: the sum of projectHours(range) against the sum of weekTotals(W). Equal totals don't show that both reads use the same scope, because different week sets can add up to the same number. The test is also only valid if `range` covers exactly the days of W, including weekend entries. Fix: compare per-week or per-project breakdowns, or assert the set of visible week ids, rather than one sum.
findings.scenario: Viewer X can see week A (10 h) in one read and week B (10 h) in the other. Both reads total 20 h and the test passes.

findings.message: The audit check counts every `time.week.locked_change` row in `core.audit_event`, with no filter on tenant, resource or actor, and expects exactly 1. Any other test in the suite that makes a locked change before this one, or a different test order, breaks it. A wrong row can also satisfy it. Fix: filter on the resource (Maya's 2026-W43 week id) and the actor (Sahan), and assert the count goes up by one.
findings.scenario: A later-added test makes another Admin locked change in the same DB first. The count is 2 and the test fails, even though the behaviour is correct.

findings.message: parts.tsx is a shared UI helper file (STATUS, initials, avatar, DAY_NAMES). It now imports `../server/weeks`, which is server code that reaches the DB layer, and also `next/navigation`. If any `"use client"` component in the module imports parts.tsx, for example Timesheets with its client-side CSV export, the server module gets bundled into the client, which is an NX1 blocker. I couldn't read the module sources in this session to confirm either way. Fix: move weekParam into a server-only file used only by MyPage and TeamPage, and keep parts.tsx free of server imports.
findings.scenario: A client component imports `{ STATUS }` from './parts'. The client bundle now pulls in server/weeks and @amax/db, and the build either fails or ships server code.

findings.message: weekParam's bare `catch {}` turns every exception from wantedWeek into a 404, not only the refusal of a bad week key. A bug or unexpected failure then shows as 'not found' instead of an error. Fix: catch only the specific error wantedWeek throws for bad input, and rethrow anything else.
findings.scenario: wantedWeek throws a TypeError from a regression. The user sees a 404 for a valid week URL, and nothing is logged as an error.

findings.message: The 'no UTC today' guard matches only three exact spellings. Other ways of getting a calendar day from server time slip past it: `new Date().toISOString().split("T")[0]`, `new Date(Date.now()).toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, `toLocaleDateString(...)` with no timeZone, a helper named `todayIso`/`now()`, and `const today = new Date()`. That makes it a check on the instance, not the class. Fix: flag any `toISOString()` or no-argument `new Date()`/`Date.now()` in non-test source and keep an explicit allowlist, or route 'today' through one helper that takes the viewer's time zone and ban the rest.
findings.scenario: Someone adds `const day = a.day ?? new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` to server/log.ts → the guard test stays green and UTC-day logging comes back.

findings.message: remindWeek always returns `delivered: false` and the 'nothing delivers it' note, even when notifications (030) is installed and has a rule for weekReminded. The result states a delivery outcome the service never checks. Fix: base the field and note on `hasModule('notifications')` (module standard, optional integrations), or drop `delivered` and say only `recorded: true`.
findings.scenario: Notifications is installed with a weekReminded rule → the MCP agent reads delivered:false, follows the tool description, and messages the person itself → the person gets two reminders.

findings.message: The fix removes the 'today' marker from the week chart label and from weekSpan instead of computing it where the viewer's day is known (a small client component that uses the browser's local date). That changes the screen against the mock. The module standard says screen changes are proposed in their own small change, so record this deviation or render the marker on the client.
findings.scenario: A user opens Team time for the current week → the mock shows 'Wed, today' and '(today, in progress)', the app shows neither.
